CVX.rationale: CVX presents a deeply unattractive fundamental picture. Trailing earnings have collapsed — Q1 2026 EPS diluted of $1.11 is down -44.5% YoY, net income down -34.7% YoY, and operating cash flow down -51.6% YoY. The trailing PE has nearly doubled from ~16x to ~32.8x while ROE has halved from 10.5% to 5.9%, representing a severe decoupling of price from deteriorating fundamentals. The 3.1% earnings yield sits 135bp below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.45%, removing the traditional valuation rationale for owning an energy major. While the qual report notes a ~14x forward P/E implying consensus expects an earnings recovery, this recovery is highly contingent on oil prices remaining elevated — and WTI has already retreated from $114.58 to $91.58, with further downside risk if geopolitical tensions ease. The Hess acquisition added ~$37B in liabilities while cash generation collapsed, and the Guyana arbitration with ExxonMobil represents a genuine tail risk to the deal's value. Berkshire Hathaway's 35% stake reduction signals institutional concern. The near-term catalyst picture is negative: if U.S.-Iran ceasefire holds, crude falls further and CVX declines; the binary oil-price leverage makes this a high-risk, low-margin-of-safety position. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, stretched trailing valuation, and unfavorable near-term risk/reward — align bearishly.
